text:
The week opens in the middle of the pattern Jordan has been tracking for a while now: work delivers a blow, and the withdrawal follows automatically. On the 24th it's Marcus's flat, corporate delivery of the restructuring news — "under evaluation," "continue executing" — that sends Jordan home at 4pm without a word to anyone, blinds shut, cancelling on Dev with a cover story about being busy. The couch, Pepper's weight, and eventually Mika showing up uninvited with pad thai are what pull the gears loose again. Jordan names the mechanism plainly: work knocks me down, I withdraw, someone from outside has to come pull me back, and that someone is always Mika.

The 25th is a genuine high point, almost a counterweight to the 24th. At Groundwork — now enough of a routine that the barista knows the order — Jordan cracks the design problem on Coda's free-play mode, building a working prototype in ninety minutes. Mika stopping by to plan another open mic, and Jordan saying yes instantly, reads as evidence that the low from Monday didn't calcify. Jordan explicitly reframes the job as one thread among several — Coda, Dev, Mika, music, Pepper, the apartment — rather than the whole fabric, though notes this is a realization that keeps needing to be re-arrived-at rather than one that sticks.

The 27th moves the pattern forward rather than just naming it: Jordan goes back and tells Dev the truth about Monday's cancellation instead of letting the excuse stand. The anxiety of typing and deleting it four times, and Dev's response — grateful, and matched with their own admission of disappearing into the bass — becomes a small but real expansion of who's allowed to see Jordan struggling. Jordan articulates the deeper mechanics of the withdrawal clearly here: protecting the appearance of being fine is what prolongs the withdrawal, and Mika's exemption from this was earned through history that Dev doesn't have yet, so extending that same access to Dev has to be a deliberate act rather than something assumed.

The 28th introduces a new thread that complicates the "job is just one thread" reframe: Lena's last day, and her offer to refer Jordan to Northlight. Jordan's reflexive response — "I don't think I'd have good enough experience" — surprises Jordan in the moment, precisely because it contradicts what Jordan knows to be true about their own work (the dashboard project, already validated in an earlier entry). The self-diminishment isn't a considered belief, it's an automatic reflex that beats sincerity to the microphone. This is unresolved going into next week: the referral is pending on Lena's end, Jordan's reflexive self-doubt is now visible but not addressed, and Monday will be the first day at Meridian without Lena there to make bad meetings survivable.
